assessment.report:
# Efficient test execution: final scoped assessment (0.9.3)

## Reviewed scope and implementation

The approved default applies to Codex-run development/testing of all products, not only products containing AI. The shared test contract selects an adequate low-observation-cost entrypoint, lets repeatable runners execute actions/assertions/fixtures/cleanup, and makes Agent observation summary-first with required failure, ambiguous, unexpected and material/safety evidence drill-down. Full trustworthy, redacted results remain available; unchecked, skipped, timed-out or failed work cannot inherit a pass. No measured saving claim is made.

API/integration carries broad business-rule, authentication, data/state and failure permutations; browser testing retains representative complete user journeys and distinct UI/client/front-to-backend risks. Equivalent conditions/assertions/results and per-case evidence justify avoiding duplicate proposed browser permutations, not a test-count ratio or universal API superset. Client-only/duplicated rules and rendered visual requirements retain their own evidence. Only a declared complete real application boundary can establish API E2E; narrow endpoints, mocks and direct model calls are not substitutes. Manual-to-E2E mapping, TDD and user-only acceptance/archival remain intact. No API, production seam, simulator, platform or architectural refactor is imposed.

The canonical rule lives in test-acceptance-contract; five Skill entrypoints reference it, execution templates expose planning/outcome fields, and Initialize emits the six-field planning table before the existing coverage mapping. No runtime parser/schema/policyVersion, model profile or installed payload changed. VERSION, CHANGELOG, README current-release reference and documentation.ps1 Kit provenance agree on0.9.3 as a patch extension, without stable promotion. README contains only stable summary/navigation; this scope's canonical packet owns actual results and pending human verification. Architecture is adequate as-is; no applicable PRD or OpenSpec marker was found. Unrelated inventoried documents remain unchanged and are not recertified.

## Actual evidence and limitations

Lead read the original contracts, source/template/tests, architecture, README and version policy; scoped readiness and initial Tester packet Validate passed before writer release. Tester observed the new table invariant fail exit1 before implementation with fixture cleanup, then pass exit0 on the completed draft. Native validation and five isolated stage, validation, documentation, fake-home install and deployment suites all passed and removed owned fixtures. New tests check emitted fields and read-only byte preservation/legacy compatibility/manual-pending archive rejection, not normative wording. Tester inspected comments against assertions and semantically walked ET-01 through ET-07. Reviewer independently inspected the actual coherent diff and packet, found no material defects and independently passed native/packet validation and whitespace checks. Lead inspected final evidence and corrected an outdated isolated-result label without changing real-workflow/manual status.

Actual selected-role roster: /root/efficient_test_tester (team-tester), /root/efficient_test_writer (team-docs-maintainer), /root/efficient_test_reviewer (team-reviewer), all complete. Exact roles were available in the active tool catalog before selection; no retries, failed creations, generic substitutes or child recursion. Returned handles do not independently confirm loaded identity/model/effort, which remain unknown. Source/tool expectations were not substituted for inference evidence.

The optional skill-creator Python quick helper could not start because yaml was unavailable. No dependency installation or Skill failure is inferred; native package frontmatter/naming/resource validation is the available substitute. Actual Codex target-workflow E2E, user manual acceptance and matched token savings remain unobserved/pending in docs/verification/active/efficient-test-execution.md. Source interpretation and script validation are not those passes. No real install, product edit, external service call, commit, push or stable selection occurred. This review certifies sufficient inspected inputs for the bounded task, not whole-project correctness or future Agent adherence.
